title: NSUI members protest at Delhi police station over alleged assault
seoTitle: Delhi NSUI protest over alleged assault

tea.why: NSUI members are protesting against the alleged assault of their women workers by a Delhi Police officer.
tea.want: The registration of an FIR against the accused police officer and an impartial investigation into the alleged assault.
tea.changed: Oct 15: The Delhi Police detained the NSUI president and several members during a protest at the Parliament Street Police Station.

summary: On October 15, 2026, members of the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) staged a protest at the Parliament Street Police Station in New Delhi. The demonstration followed allegations that NSUI women workers were assaulted by a female police officer. The organisation claimed that despite approaching senior officials, no FIR had been registered regarding the incident. NSUI president Vinod Jakhar alleged that the women were taken to a dark room and attacked. During the protest, the Delhi Police detained Jakhar and several other members. The NSUI leadership condemned the detentions, accusing the police of shielding officials and acting under political influence. The organisation stated it would continue to protest until its demands for an FIR and an investigation are met.
demands: Registration of an FIR against the accused police officer
Impartial investigation into the alleged assault
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: NSUI members protested at Parliament Street Police Station demanding an FIR for the alleged assault of women workers.
Delhi Police detained the NSUI president and several members during the demonstration.
